A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EIC symbolic-regression work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison; internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original SRBench experiments, generative-model training results, formula-distribution analyses, and human and LLM preference evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and additionally reports structural-stability measurements for LLM-SRBench formulas in Appendix C.1.

M1.justification: V1 computes EIC through stochastic perturbations at operator nodes. V2 adds a deterministic condition-number recursion and revises the stochastic estimator to perturb leaf nodes and use log standard-deviation amplification rather than log variance amplification (Algorithms 1–2). These change the documented computation, while the GP/MCTS penalty and pretraining-filtering schemes remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds structural evaluation of 111 Transform and 129 Synth formulas from LLM-SRBench (Appendix C.1), extending coverage to transformed and LLM-synthesized expressions. The existing SRBench tasks, named-equation datasets, and 19 human-evaluation problems remain.

E2.justification: The black-box comparison plots add PySR and RSRM and remove MRGP, FFX, and ITEA (v1 Figure 6 versus v2 Figures 4 and 9). FEAT also appears in the revised plots but was already evaluated in v1 Table 7. The white-box comparator set and PhyE2E pretraining comparison remain.

E3.justification: Besides revising the EIC evaluation metric, v2 changes human-study selection from EIC-MCTS/PySR pairs to pooled search-method formulas and lowers the minimum EIC difference from 3 to 2. Section 4.4 changes valid evaluations from 840 to 870, although Appendix C.4 retains 840. Table 1 changes the Wiki sample count from 940 to 984, while Appendix C.3 retains 940. Pretraining is now described as plateauing at approximately five million samples rather than remaining plateaued over five million, despite unchanged Table 2 training counts. These are reported changes, not evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a diagnostic comparison of instability in physical, algebraically transformed, and LLM-synthesized formulas, examining whether transformation and synthesis are associated with less stable structures. Existing noise-robustness tests, EIC-guidance comparisons, and pretraining-distribution analyses remain; relocating their plots does not add analyses.

E5.justification: V2 first reports a human-preference 95% confidence interval of [67%, 73%], a one-sided binomial test with p < 10^-30, and Fleiss' kappa of 0.37. This substantially expands statistical assessment of the central interpretability validation. The existing ten search trials and repeated LLM ratings remain unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds mean EIC results of 0.848, 1.456, and 2.811 for SRBench, Transform, and Synth formulas, respectively (Figure 7). Human preference changes from 70.12% in v1 Section 4.4 to 69.8% under the revised selection protocol, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Existing score values in Tables 1–7 are retained, while black-box plots change result membership and associated ranks.

T1.justification: V2 introduces an explicit multiplicative-noise assumption, Proposition 3.2 and its recursive error-propagation proof, and derivations concerning unit invariance, algebraic rewriting, precision loss, and signal-to-noise degradation (Appendix A.1–A.6). Its standard-deviation formulation also corrects the missing factor of one-half in v1's variance-to-significant-digits identity. This substantially revises the mathematical foundation.

C1.justification: The central Pareto-front, pretraining-efficiency, and interpretability-alignment contributions remain. However, v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion strengthen the interpretation of human agreement into a claim that structural stability is a critical prerequisite for interpretability, rather than merely evidence that EIC reflects interpretability.

C2.justification: V2 reattributes DSR/RSRM stability to hard structural constraints, whereas v1 emphasized dimensional constraints for DSR. It recasts GP's black-box accuracy loss as sacrificing unstable approximation for physical plausibility and adds explanations linking transformed-formula instability to inversion and small denominators. These materially revise the mechanisms used to interpret results; the existing phase-transition applicability caveat remains.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the derivative-capable engine required by analytical computation and double-precision reference calculations for stochastic estimation. Conversely, it removes v1 Appendix A.1's concrete noise scale of 10^-6, requiring only a sufficiently small scale. Search weights, filtering threshold, and pretraining hyperparameter grids remain documented as before.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around evaluation metrics and constraints, discussing SRBench++, SRSD, LLM-SRBench, Pareto-optimal evaluation, and expert assessment. It adds LLM-guided search, variable-selection, quantization, and Occam's-razor references while shortening the earlier genetic-programming citation catalog. EIC is more explicitly positioned as addressing structural properties missed by input-output and complexity evaluations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, and experimental interpretations are extensively rewritten around structural stability. Search and filtering explanations move into the experimental sections, and the appendices are reorganized into theory, methodology details, and results. An impact statement is added.

P2.justification: V2 removes the workflow schematic, adds a noise-amplification axis to Figure 2, redraws the complexity/EIC comparison, and combines the main Pareto plots while moving their EIC panels to Appendix Figure 9. It adds two LLM-formula plots and an analytical algorithm display, relabels human comparisons as lower/higher EIC, and reformats tables. The evaluation-interface screenshots and LLM prompt are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies EIC's mathematics, corrects its variance-to-digits factor, and adds useful stability and human-agreement analyses. However, normalization and leaf perturbations change while the existing EIC tables and penalty/filter thresholds remain unchanged, without explaining which formulation produced those results. The revised human study also reports 870 valid evaluations in Section 4.4 but 840 in Appendix C.4. These unresolved links between the revised method and its empirical support prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
